title: My Boss Wanted Every Email. He Got Every Email.
script: My boss wanted every email. He announced that nobody could send anything without copying him because he needed 'complete visibility'—his exact phrase. Fine. I updated every automated alert, calendar notice, shared-document comment, delivery receipt, and ticket notification to include him. Nothing fake—just the messages our systems already generated all day. By lunch, his inbox had hundreds. By Wednesday, he missed a client's urgent approval because it was buried between a printer alert and twelve calendar updates. Complete visibility had become complete camouflage. He called me in and asked why I had flooded him. I showed him his own written rule and the audit log proving every message was legitimate. He quietly changed the policy to 'copy me only on decisions requiring approval.' I followed that one too. His inbox recovered, the client's request got handled, and the new rule lasted. Apparently visibility works better when you can still see.
